name: cite
comment: The cite operation of the annotation facet (app/src/PrismCite.lex.tex): from a reply's address and, for each of its placeholders, where it starts and ends in the reply's text, the address of the item it was filled from and the exact text taken, the citations of that reply as W3C Web Annotations. A request is the reply's address and a line end, then per citation '<start> <end> <item address> <n>', a line end, the n bytes of the exact text and a line end; an address is 'sha256:' and 64 lower-case hex digits. The answer is a JSON array in RFC 8785 form, one annotation per citation: its motivation is linking, its target a Specific Resource on the reply selected by a TextPositionSelector (Recommendation 4.2.5), its body a Specific Resource on the item selected by a TextQuoteSelector (4.2.4), its id 'sha256:' and the SHA-256 of the annotation without an id. An annotation is answered only when the annotation judge (PrismAnnotation, held to the web-platform-tests annotation-model suite) finds every annotationMusts assertion as the suite expects; otherwise, and for a request not of this form, the answer is invalid. 'examples' are the acceptance vectors. No expected answer is the model's own output: each is built outside LexLean as an object of that shape, written by the RFC 8785 author's canonicalizer ('canonicalizer'), addressed by SHA-256 and accepted by the suite's own validator ('suite' in app/specs/annotation/spec.json). The exact texts and positions are the TextQuoteSelector and TextPositionSelector values of the W3C documents pinned there and the strings of the RFC 8785 author's test data (app/specs/oracle/json-canonicalization); the addresses are digests of NIST's SHA-256 short messages (app/specs/oracle/nist-cavp-sha256). The last three examples are refusals the request form itself defines: an end before its start, an address that is not sha256, a text shorter than its stated length.
